transcript.content: Hello, welcome. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because my eating has been getting kind of out of hand. After work or class, I’ll sit down with my laptop and start eating, and it turns into way more than I meant to have—like a whole takeout meal, then chips or sweets, and sometimes whatever snacks I have in my desk drawer. It’s definitely more than I’d eat if someone else were around.
When you find yourself eating that way, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yeah. Once I start, it really does feel like I can’t stop. I’ll be sitting there thinking, like, Jaime, stop, you have a budget report to finish, and I’m not even enjoying it anymore… but I still keep reaching for the next thing.
Does this kind of eating cause you a lot of distress, or does it interfere with things like work, relationships, or how you see yourself?

Yeah, it does. I’ve been skipping plans with friends and family, like cooking nights and stuff, because I’m worried they’ll notice or somehow realize how much I’ve been eating when I’m alone. So I’ve been keeping to myself more outside of work and school, and that feels pretty bad.
Do you usually end up eating this way alone because you’re embarrassed about how much you’re eating?

Yeah. I usually wait until my roommate is out, or until my family has gone to bed. I feel embarrassed for anyone to see how much I can eat, especially because during the day I try to act really put-together and health-conscious.
After these episodes of eating more than you plan to, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise a lot more than usual to try to balance it out?
I don’t really know. I mean, I don’t think I do those things… I haven’t noticed myself doing that after. Usually I just feel bad and try to move on.
During these episodes, do you feel like you’re completely losing control, like you can’t stop eating no matter how hard you try?

Yeah. Once I start, it really does feel like I can’t stop. I’ll be thinking, like, “Jaime, stop, you have work to finish,” or I know I’m not even enjoying it anymore, but I still keep reaching for the next thing. It feels like I’m kind of watching myself do it.
After these eating episodes, do you find yourself feeling guilty, ashamed, or disgusted with yourself?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I don’t feel good afterward, but I haven’t really sat and separated out whether it’s guilt or shame or something else. I usually just feel bad and try not to think about it too much.
Do these episodes of eating happen more when you're feeling stressed, sad, or upset?
I’m not totally sure. I haven’t really tracked it that way. Sometimes I’m stressed, but I can’t say for sure that’s what sets it off.
How often do these episodes of eating more than you plan to and feeling out of control happen in a week?

When I looked back at my journal and even my food delivery charges, it’s been happening most weeks. Usually more than once a week, not just like a random one-time thing here or there. It’s been like that since the restructuring started.

Can you tell me more about how these eating episodes affect your daily life? Specifically, do they interfere with your ability to focus at work, attend school, or engage in activities you used to enjoy?

Yeah, it does affect things, mostly outside of work and school. I’ve been avoiding plans with friends and family, especially things like cooking nights or meals together, because I’m worried they’ll notice how much I’ve been eating on my own. So I end up staying home more and feeling kind of isolated.
Do these eating episodes themselves cause you a lot of distress, regardless of how you feel afterward?
I’m not sure how to separate that, honestly. During it, I mostly just feel like I’m not really in control, but I don’t always think of it as “distress” until after. Then I feel really upset about it.
Can you describe what goes through your mind right before you start eating this way—do you feel a strong urge or compulsion to eat, even if you're not hungry?

Yeah. A lot of the time it’s after I’ve already eaten dinner, so I’m not actually hungry. But my mind feels restless, and I keep thinking about going back to the kitchen or ordering something else. It feels like this strong pull to eat even though my body doesn’t need it.

Have you ever felt so upset or distressed about these eating episodes that you changed your routine significantly, or have you ever tried to hide how much you’re eating by throwing food away or eating in secret?

Yeah… I’ve definitely tried to hide it. I’ll wait until my roommate is out, or if I’m at home, until my family has gone to bed. It’s embarrassing, because during the day I act like I have everything together and like I’m health-conscious, and then later I can eat way more than I’d ever want anyone to see.

Do you feel a lot of emotional discomfort or distress specifically about the fact that these eating episodes are happening, even aside from how they affect your social plans or how you feel afterward?

I don’t know if I can separate it that clearly. I don’t like that it happens, and I feel uncomfortable thinking about it, but the really strong upset feeling usually hits after. During or before, it’s more like I’m caught up in it than sitting there feeling distressed about the fact that it’s happening.
